To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The procedural system is sensitive to the reliability of feedback and the frequency of training trials; 2) The declarative system is sensitive to feedback valence, but not frequency; 3) Both systems are sensitive to feedback latency; and 4) The procedural system, but not the RB system, is sensitive to the complexity of the category structure.

(1) the procedural system is slow and incremental, and it is highly sensitive to reliable feedback; (2) the procedural system can learn many different types of category structures; (3) the RB system is fast and can learn a limited set of category structures; and (4) the two systems can learn in parallel, with the declarative RB system suppressing the procedural system as long as the declarative system is successful.

(1) there are multiple systems of learning, (2) these systems compete throughout learning, and (3) the declarative RB system learns quickly, but only for a small set of category structure, whereas the procedural system is slow but learns a wide variety of structures.
